1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * BK7258 CPU2 startup.
3:  ****************************************************************************/
4: 
5: #include <nuttx/config.h>
6: 
7: #include <assert.h>
8: #include <errno.h>
9: #include <stdbool.h>
10: #include <stdint.h>
11: #include <syslog.h>
12: 
13: #include <nuttx/arch.h>
14: #include <nuttx/atomic.h>
15: #include <nuttx/clock.h>
16: #include <nuttx/sched.h>
17: #include <nuttx/sched_note.h>
18: 
19: #include "arm_internal.h"
20: #include "dwt.h"
21: #include "init/init.h"
22: #include "nvic.h"
23: #include "sched/sched.h"
24: #include "hardware/bk7258_memorymap.h"
25: #include "hardware/bk7258_mbox.h"
26: #include "hardware/bk7258_sysctrl.h"
27: #include "bk7258_boottrace.h"
28: #include "bk7258_smp.h"
29: 
30: #if CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS != 2
31: #  error "BK7258 OpenVela SMP supports exactly two AP CPUs"
32: #endif
33: 
34: #if CONFIG_BK7258_CPU_FREQ_HZ != 480000000
35: #  error "BK7258 OpenVela SMP requires the fixed 480 MHz CP contract"
36: #endif
37: 
38: #define BK7258_CPU2_ONLINE_CYCLES  (CONFIG_BK7258_CPU_FREQ_HZ / 2u)
39: #define BK7258_CPU2_POLL_LIMIT     4000000u
40: 
41: extern uint8_t __secondary_vectors_start[];
42: extern uint8_t __secondary_boot_stack_base[];
43: 
44: static void bk7258_cpu2_hold_reset(void)
45: {
46:   putreg32(getreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL) & ~BK7258_CPU2_RESET_RELEASE,
47:            BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL);
48:   UP_DSB();
49: }
50: 
51: static void bk7258_cpu2_release_reset(void)
52: {
53:   putreg32(getreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL) | BK7258_CPU2_RESET_RELEASE,
54:            BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL);
55:   UP_DSB();
56:   __asm__ volatile("sev" ::: "memory");
57: }
58: 
59: static void __attribute__((used, noreturn)) bk7258_secondary_idle(void)
60: {
61:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_IDLE);
62:   arm_initialize_stack();
63:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_STACK);
64:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_ONLINE);
65:   bk7258_smp_boot_notify();
66:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_NOTIFY);
67:   up_irq_enable();
68:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_IRQ_ON);
69:   sched_note_cpu_started(this_task());
70:   nx_idle_trampoline();
71:   PANIC();
72: }
73: 
74: static void __attribute__((naked, noreturn))
75: bk7258_secondary_enter(uintptr_t idle_top __attribute__((unused)),
76:                        uintptr_t idle_base __attribute__((unused)))
77: {
78:   __asm__ volatile
79:     (
80:       "msr psp, r0\n"
81: #ifdef CONFIG_ARMV8M_STACKCHECK_HARDWARE
82:       "msr psplim, r1\n"
83: #endif
84:       "mrs r1, control\n"
85:       "orr r1, r1, #2\n"
86:       "msr control, r1\n"
87:       "isb sy\n"
88:       "b bk7258_secondary_idle\n"
89:     );
90: }
91: 
92: static void __attribute__((used, noinline, noreturn,
93:                            target("general-regs-only")))
94: bk7258_secondary_boot(void)
95: {
96:   struct tcb_s *tcb;
97:   uintptr_t idle_top;
98: 
99:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_ENTRY);
100:   bk7258_cpu_private_initialize(false);
101:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_PRIVATE);
102:   bk7258_irqinitialize_secondary();
103:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_IRQ);
104:   if (bk7258_mbox_secondary_init() < 0)
105:     {
106:       PANIC();
107:     }
108: 
109:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_MBOX);
110: 
111:   tcb = current_task(1);
112:   idle_top = ((uintptr_t)tcb->stack_base_ptr + tcb->adj_stack_size) & ~7u;
113:   bk7258_secondary_enter(idle_top, (uintptr_t)tcb->stack_base_ptr);
114: }
115: 
116: void __attribute__((naked, noreturn, section(".start_text")))
117: bk7258_secondary_start(void)
118: {
119:   __asm__ volatile
120:     (
121:       "cpsid i\n"
122:       "movs r0, #1\n"
123:       "ldr r1, =0x20000000\n"
124:       "str r0, [r1]\n"
125:       "ldr r0, =__secondary_boot_stack_base\n"
126:       "msr msplim, r0\n"
127:       "b bk7258_secondary_boot\n"
128:     );
129: }
130: 
131: int up_cpu_start(int cpu)
132: {
133:   irqstate_t flags;
134:   uint32_t started;
135:   uint32_t polls = 0;
136:   uint32_t control;
137:   uint32_t status;
138:   bool ping_sent = false;
139: 
140:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_ENTER);
141: 
142:   if (cpu != 1 || this_cpu() != 0)
143:     {
144:       return -EINVAL;
145:     }
146: 
147:   status = getreg32(BK7258_CPU_RUN_STATUS);
148:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(0, status);
149:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(1, bk7258_mbox_smp_ready());
150:   if ((status & BK7258_CPU_STATUS_CPU2_POWER_DOWN) != 0 ||
151:       !bk7258_mbox_smp_ready())
152:     {
153:       syslog(LOG_ERR, "CPU2 prerequisite failed: status=%08lx mbox=%u\n",
154:              (unsigned long)status, bk7258_mbox_smp_ready());
155:       PANIC();
156:     }
157: 
158:   bk7258_cpu2_hold_reset();
159:   control = getreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL);
160:   status = getreg32(BK7258_CPU_RUN_STATUS);
161:   if ((control & BK7258_CPU2_RESET_RELEASE) != 0 ||
162:       (status & BK7258_CPU_STATUS_CPU2_RESET) != 0)
163:     {
164:       syslog(LOG_ERR, "CPU2 reset hold failed: ctrl=%08lx status=%08lx\n",
165:              (unsigned long)control, (unsigned long)status);
166:       PANIC();
167:     }
168: 
169:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_HELD);
170:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(0, control);
171:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(1, status);
172: 
173:   bk7258_smp_prepare_boot();
174:   putreg32(0, BK7258_CPU2_IRQ_EN0);
175:   putreg32(0, BK7258_CPU2_IRQ_EN1);
176:   modifyreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL, BK7258_CPU2_OFFSET_MASK,
177:               BK7258_CPU2_RXEVT_SEL |
178:               (((uintptr_t)__secondary_vectors_start >> 8) <<
179:                BK7258_CPU2_OFFSET_SHIFT));
180:   UP_DMB();
181:   UP_DSB();
182: 
183:   putreg32(getreg32(NVIC_DEMCR) | NVIC_DEMCR_TRCENA, NVIC_DEMCR);
184:   putreg32(0, DWT_CYCCNT);
185:   putreg32(getreg32(DWT_CTRL) | DWT_CTRL_CYCCNTENA_MASK, DWT_CTRL);
186:   started = getreg32(DWT_CYCCNT);
187:   flags = up_irq_save();
188:   bk7258_cpu2_release_reset();
189:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_RELEASED);
190:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(0, getreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL));
191:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(1, getreg32(BK7258_CPU_RUN_STATUS));
192: 
193:   while (!bk7258_smp_boot_test_complete())
194:     {
195:       bk7258_mbox_kick_rx();
196:       if (bk7258_smp_boot_notified() && !ping_sent)
197:         {
198:           if (bk7258_smp_boot_ping(1) < 0)
199:             {
200:               break;
201:             }
202: 
203:           ping_sent = true;
204:           bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_ONLINE);
205:         }
206: 
207:       if (getreg32(DWT_CYCCNT) - started >= BK7258_CPU2_ONLINE_CYCLES ||
208:           ++polls >= BK7258_CPU2_POLL_LIMIT)
209:         {
210:           break;
211:         }
212:     }
213: 
214:   if (!bk7258_smp_boot_test_complete())
215:     {
216:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(0, getreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL));
217:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(1, getreg32(BK7258_CPU_RUN_STATUS));
218:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(2, getreg32(BK7258_MBOX_CH1_STATUS));
219:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(3, getreg32(BK7258_MBOX_CH2_STATUS));
220:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(4, ping_sent);
221:       bk7258_cpu2_hold_reset();
222:       up_irq_restore(flags);
223:       syslog(LOG_ERR,
224:              "CPU2 online timeout: ctrl=%08lx status=%08lx fifo=%08lx/%08lx ping=%u\n",
225:              (unsigned long)getreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL),
226:              (unsigned long)getreg32(BK7258_CPU_RUN_STATUS),
227:              (unsigned long)getreg32(BK7258_MBOX_CH1_STATUS),
228:              (unsigned long)getreg32(BK7258_MBOX_CH2_STATUS), ping_sent);
229:       PANIC();
230:     }
231: 
232:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_IPI_DONE);
233:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(2, UINT32_MAX);
234:   putreg32(1u << (BK7258_EXTIRQ_MAILBOX & 31),
235:            NVIC_IRQ_CLRPEND(BK7258_EXTIRQ_MAILBOX));
236:   UP_DSB();
237:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_IRQ_RESTORE);
238:   up_irq_restore(flags);
239:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_IRQ_RETURN);
240:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_START_DONE);
241:   return OK;
242: }

1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_irq.c
3:  *
4:  * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
5:  ****************************************************************************/
6: 
7: #include <nuttx/config.h>
8: 
9: #include <stdint.h>
10: 
11: #include <nuttx/arch.h>
12: #include <nuttx/irq.h>
13: 
14: #include <arch/arm_m/nvicpri.h>
15: 
16: #include "arm_internal.h"
17: #include "nvic.h"
18: 
19: #include "hardware/bk7258_sysctrl.h"
20: #include "bk7258_boottrace.h"
21: 
22: #define DEFPRIORITY32 \
23:   (NVIC_SYSH_PRIORITY_DEFAULT << 24 | \
24:    NVIC_SYSH_PRIORITY_DEFAULT << 16 | \
25:    NVIC_SYSH_PRIORITY_DEFAULT << 8  | \
26:     NVIC_SYSH_PRIORITY_DEFAULT)
27: 
28: static inline void bk7258_prioritize_svcall(int priority);
29: 
30: static inline void bk7258_route_irq(int extirq, bool enable)
31: {
32:   uintptr_t regaddr;
33:   uint32_t bit;
34:   int cpu = up_cpu_index();
35: 
36: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
37:   if (cpu == 1 && extirq != BK7258_IRQ_MAILBOX - BK7258_IRQ_FIRST)
38:     {
39:       return;
40:     }
41: #endif
42: 
43:   if (extirq < 32)
44:     {
45:       regaddr = cpu == 0 ? BK7258_CPU1_IRQ_EN0 : BK7258_CPU2_IRQ_EN0;
46:       bit = 1u << extirq;
47:     }
48:   else
49:     {
50:       regaddr = cpu == 0 ? BK7258_CPU1_IRQ_EN1 : BK7258_CPU2_IRQ_EN1;
51:       bit = 1u << (extirq - 32);
52:     }
53: 
54:   if (enable)
55:     {
56:       modifyreg32(regaddr, 0, bit);
57:     }
58:   else
59:     {
60:       modifyreg32(regaddr, bit, 0);
61:     }
62: }
63: 
64: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
65: void bk7258_irqinitialize_secondary(void)
66: {
67:   uintptr_t regaddr;
68:   int priority_registers;
69:   int i;
70: 
71:   for (i = 0; i < BK7258_EXTIRQ_COUNT; i += 32)
72:     {
73:       putreg32(0xffffffffu, NVIC_IRQ_CLEAR(i));
74:       putreg32(0xffffffffu, NVIC_IRQ_CLRPEND(i));
75:     }
76: 
77:   putreg32(0, BK7258_CPU2_IRQ_EN0);
78:   putreg32(0, BK7258_CPU2_IRQ_EN1);
79:   putreg32(0, NVIC_SYSTICK_CTRL);
80: 
81:   putreg32(DEFPRIORITY32, NVIC_SYSH4_7_PRIORITY);
82:   putreg32(DEFPRIORITY32, NVIC_SYSH8_11_PRIORITY);
83:   putreg32(DEFPRIORITY32, NVIC_SYSH12_15_PRIORITY);
84: 
85:   priority_registers = ((getreg32(NVIC_ICTR) & 0x1f) + 1) * 8;
86:   regaddr = NVIC_IRQ0_3_PRIORITY;
87:   while (priority_registers-- > 0)
88:     {
89:       putreg32(DEFPRIORITY32, regaddr);
90:       regaddr += 4;
91:     }
92: 
93:   bk7258_prioritize_svcall(NVIC_SYSH_SVCALL_PRIORITY);
94:   modifyreg32(NVIC_SYSHCON, 0,
95:               NVIC_SYSHCON_MEMFAULTENA | NVIC_SYSHCON_BUSFAULTENA |
96:               NVIC_SYSHCON_USGFAULTENA | NVIC_SYSHCON_SECUREFAULTENA);
97: }
98: #endif
99: 
100: static int bk7258_irqinfo(int irq, uintptr_t *regaddr, uint32_t *bit,
101:                           uintptr_t offset)
102: {
103:   int extirq;
104: 
105:   DEBUGASSERT(irq >= BK7258_IRQ_NMI && irq < NR_IRQS);
106: 
107:   if (irq >= BK7258_IRQ_FIRST)
108:     {
109:       extirq = irq - BK7258_IRQ_FIRST;
110:       *regaddr = NVIC_IRQ_ENABLE(extirq) + offset;
111:       *bit = 1u << (extirq & 31);
112:       return OK;
113:     }
114: 
115:   *regaddr = NVIC_SYSHCON;
116:   switch (irq)
117:     {
118:       case BK7258_IRQ_MEMFAULT:
119:         *bit = NVIC_SYSHCON_MEMFAULTENA;
120:         break;
121:       case BK7258_IRQ_BUSFAULT:
122:         *bit = NVIC_SYSHCON_BUSFAULTENA;
123:         break;
124:       case BK7258_IRQ_USAGEFAULT:
125:         *bit = NVIC_SYSHCON_USGFAULTENA;
126:         break;
127:       case BK7258_IRQ_SECUREFAULT:
128:         *bit = NVIC_SYSHCON_SECUREFAULTENA;
129:         break;
130:       case BK7258_IRQ_SYSTICK:
131:         *regaddr = NVIC_SYSTICK_CTRL;
132:         *bit = NVIC_SYSTICK_CTRL_ENABLE;
133:         break;
134:       default:
135:         return ERROR;
136:     }
137: 
138:   return OK;
139: }
140: 
141: static inline void bk7258_prioritize_svcall(int priority)
142: {
143:   uint32_t regval = getreg32(NVIC_SYSH8_11_PRIORITY);
144:   regval &= ~NVIC_SYSH_PRIORITY_PR11_MASK;
145:   regval |= priority << NVIC_SYSH_PRIORITY_PR11_SHIFT;
146:   putreg32(regval, NVIC_SYSH8_11_PRIORITY);
147: }
148: 
149: void up_irqinitialize(void)
150: {
151:   uintptr_t regaddr;
152:   int priority_registers;
153:   int i;
154: 
155:   for (i = 0; i < BK7258_EXTIRQ_COUNT; i += 32)
156:     {
157:       putreg32(0xffffffffu, NVIC_IRQ_CLEAR(i));
158:     }
159: 
160:   putreg32(0, BK7258_CPU1_IRQ_EN0);
161:   putreg32(0, BK7258_CPU1_IRQ_EN1);
162: 
163:   putreg32(DEFPRIORITY32, NVIC_SYSH4_7_PRIORITY);
164:   putreg32(DEFPRIORITY32, NVIC_SYSH8_11_PRIORITY);
165:   putreg32(DEFPRIORITY32, NVIC_SYSH12_15_PRIORITY);
166: 
167:   priority_registers = ((getreg32(NVIC_ICTR) & 0x1f) + 1) * 8;
168:   regaddr = NVIC_IRQ0_3_PRIORITY;
169:   while (priority_registers-- > 0)
170:     {
171:       putreg32(DEFPRIORITY32, regaddr);
172:       regaddr += 4;
173:     }
174: 
175:   irq_attach(BK7258_IRQ_SVCALL, arm_svcall, NULL);
176:   irq_attach(BK7258_IRQ_HARDFAULT, arm_hardfault, NULL);
177:   irq_attach(BK7258_IRQ_MEMFAULT, arm_memfault, NULL);
178:   irq_attach(BK7258_IRQ_BUSFAULT, arm_busfault, NULL);
179:   irq_attach(BK7258_IRQ_USAGEFAULT, arm_usagefault, NULL);
180:   irq_attach(BK7258_IRQ_SECUREFAULT, arm_securefault, NULL);
181:   arm_enable_dbgmonitor();
182:   irq_attach(BK7258_IRQ_DBGMONITOR, arm_dbgmonitor, NULL);
183: 
184:   bk7258_prioritize_svcall(NVIC_SYSH_SVCALL_PRIORITY);
185:   up_enable_irq(BK7258_IRQ_MEMFAULT);
186:   up_enable_irq(BK7258_IRQ_BUSFAULT);
187:   up_enable_irq(BK7258_IRQ_USAGEFAULT);
188:   up_enable_irq(BK7258_IRQ_SECUREFAULT);
189:   up_irq_enable();
190: }
191: 
192: void up_enable_irq(int irq)
193: {
194:   uintptr_t regaddr;
195:   uint32_t regval;
196:   uint32_t bit;
197: 
198:   if (bk7258_irqinfo(irq, &regaddr, &bit, 0) == OK)
199:     {
200:       if (irq >= BK7258_IRQ_FIRST)
201:         {
202:           bk7258_route_irq(irq - BK7258_IRQ_FIRST, true);
203:           putreg32(bit, regaddr);
204:         }
205:       else
206:         {
207:           regval = getreg32(regaddr);
208:           putreg32(regval | bit, regaddr);
209:         }
210:     }
211: }
212: 
213: void up_disable_irq(int irq)
214: {
215:   uintptr_t regaddr;
216:   uint32_t regval;
217:   uint32_t bit;
218: 
219:   if (bk7258_irqinfo(irq, &regaddr, &bit,
220:                      NVIC_IRQ0_31_CLEAR - NVIC_IRQ0_31_ENABLE) == OK)
221:     {
222:       if (irq >= BK7258_IRQ_FIRST)
223:         {
224:           putreg32(bit, regaddr);
225:           bk7258_route_irq(irq - BK7258_IRQ_FIRST, false);
226:         }
227:       else
228:         {
229:           regval = getreg32(regaddr);
230:           putreg32(regval & ~bit, regaddr);
231:         }
232:     }
233: }
234: 
235: void arm_ack_irq(int irq)
236: {
237:   if (up_cpu_index() == 0 &&
238:       bk7258_boottrace_primary_stage() == BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_IRQ_RESTORE)
239:     {
240:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(2, (uint32_t)irq);
241:       bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_FIRST_IRQ);
242:     }
243: }
244: 
245: #ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_IRQPRIO
246: int up_prioritize_irq(int irq, int priority)
247: {
248:   uintptr_t regaddr;
249:   uint32_t regval;
250:   int shift;
251: 
252:   DEBUGASSERT(irq >= BK7258_IRQ_MEMFAULT && irq < NR_IRQS);
253:   DEBUGASSERT((unsigned int)priority <= NVIC_SYSH_PRIORITY_MIN);
254: 
255:   if (irq < BK7258_IRQ_FIRST)
256:     {
257:       regaddr = NVIC_SYSH_PRIORITY(irq);
258:       irq -= 4;
259:     }
260:   else
261:     {
262:       irq -= BK7258_IRQ_FIRST;
263:       regaddr = NVIC_IRQ_PRIORITY(irq);
264:     }
265: 
266:   shift = (irq & 3) << 3;
267:   regval = getreg32(regaddr);
268:   regval &= ~(0xffu << shift);
269:   regval |= (uint32_t)priority << shift;
270:   putreg32(regval, regaddr);
271:   return OK;
272: }
273: #endif

37: {
38:   if (cpu == 0 &&
39:       bk7258_boottrace_primary_stage() == BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_FIRST_IRQ)
40:     {
41:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(4, value);
42:     }
43: }
44: 
45: static bool bk7258_hwspinlock_trylock(struct hwspinlock_dev_s *dev)
46: {
47:   unsigned int cpu = (unsigned int)up_cpu_index();
48:   unsigned int other = cpu ^ 1u;
49: 
50:   (void)dev;
51:   DEBUGASSERT(cpu < 2);
52:   bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_ENTRY);
53: 
54:   /* BK7258 has only two SRAM exclusive monitors while CP, AP CPU1 and AP
55:    * CPU2 are all active.  Keep the AP-only atomic gate independent of
56:    * LDAEX/STREX so CP traffic cannot starve an AP exclusive sequence.
57:    */
58: 
59:   /* libc atomics are normally short, but the scheduler's recursive critical
60:    * section can issue another atomic operation on the same CPU.  Re-entry
61:    * must be decided before entering Peterson arbitration; otherwise a waiter
62:    * on the other CPU can make the current owner wait for itself.
63:    */
64: 
65:   if (g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner == cpu + 1u)
66:     {
67:       if (g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth == UINT32_MAX)
68:         {
69:           PANIC();
70:         }
71: 
72:       g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth++;
73:       UP_DMB();
74:       bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_REENTER |
75:                              g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth);
76:       return true;
77:     }
78: 
79:   /* This is only a fast rejection.  The Peterson protocol below remains
80:    * authoritative while a new owner is between intent and owner publish.
81:    */
82: 
83:   if (g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner != 0)
84:     {
85:       bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_OWNER_BUSY |
86:                              g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner);
87:       return false;
88:     }
89: 
90:   /* Every attempt must publish a fresh intent and turn.  Leaving intent set
91:    * after a failed trylock makes the state stale and breaks trylock's
92:    * one-attempt contract.
93:    */
94: 
95:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[cpu] = 1;
96:   UP_DMB();
97:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.turn = other;
98:   UP_DMB();
99:   bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_INTENT);
100: 
101:   if (g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[other] != 0 &&
102:       g_bk7258_atomic_gate.turn == other)
103:     {
104:       g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[cpu] = 0;
105:       UP_DMB();
106:       __asm__ volatile("sev" ::: "memory");
107:       bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_CONFLICT);
108:       return false;
109:     }
110: 
111:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner = cpu + 1u;
112:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth = 1;
113:   UP_DMB();
114:   bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_ACQUIRED);
115:   return true;
116: }
117: 
118: static void bk7258_hwspinlock_relax(struct hwspinlock_dev_s *dev)
119: {
120:   (void)dev;
121:   __asm__ volatile("nop" ::: "memory");
122: }
123: 
124: static void bk7258_hwspinlock_unlock(struct hwspinlock_dev_s *dev)
125: {
126:   unsigned int cpu = (unsigned int)up_cpu_index();
127: 
128:   (void)dev;
129:   if (cpu >= 2 || g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner != cpu + 1u ||
130:       g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth == 0)
131:     {
132:       PANIC();
133:     }
134: 
135:   if (--g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth != 0)
136:     {
137:       UP_DMB();
138:       bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_UNLOCK |
139:                              g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth);
140:       return;
141:     }
142: 
143:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner = 0;
144:   UP_DMB();
145:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[cpu] = 0;
146:   UP_DSB();
147:   __asm__ volatile("sev" ::: "memory");
148:   bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_RELEASED);
149: }
150: 
151: const struct hwspinlock_ops_s g_bk7258_hwspinlock_ops =
152: {
153:   .trylock = bk7258_hwspinlock_trylock,
154:   .relax   = bk7258_hwspinlock_relax,
155:   .unlock  = bk7258_hwspinlock_unlock
156: };
157: 
158: void bk7258_hwspinlock_initialize(void)
159: {
160:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[0] = 0;
161:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[1] = 0;
162:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.turn = 0;
163:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner = 0;
164:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth = 0;
165:   UP_DSB();
166:   __asm__ volatile("sev" ::: "memory");
167: }

46: void exception_direct(void)
47: {
48:   int irq;
49: 
50:   up_addrenv_enter_kernel();
51:   irq = getipsr();
52: #ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_FPU
53:   __asm__ __volatile__
54:     (
55:       "mov r0, %0\n"
56:       "vmsr fpscr, r0\n"
57:       :
58:       : "i" (ARM_FPSCR_LTPSIZE_NONE)
59:     );
60: #endif
61: 
62:   arm_ack_irq(irq);
63:   irq_dispatch(irq, NULL);
64: 
65:   if (g_running_task != this_task())
66:     {
67:       up_trigger_irq(NVIC_IRQ_PENDSV, 0);
68:     }
69: 
70:   up_addrenv_leave_kernel();
71: }

73: uint32_t *arm_doirq(int irq, uint32_t *regs)
74: {
75:   struct tcb_s **running_task;
76:   struct tcb_s *tcb;
77: 
78:   up_addrenv_enter_kernel();
79:   running_task = &g_running_task;
80:   tcb = *running_task;
81: 
82:   /* This judgment proves that (*running_task)->xcp.regs
83:    * is invalid, and we can safely overwrite it.
84:    * And suspend the scheduler for the current task.
85:    */
86: 
87:   if (tcb != NULL)
88:     {
89:       tcb->xcp.regs = regs;
90:       nxsched_suspend_scheduler(tcb);
91:     }
92: 
93:   board_autoled_on(LED_INIRQ);
94: #ifdef CONFIG_SUPPRESS_INTERRUPTS
95:   PANIC();
96: #else
97: 
98:   /* Acknowledge the interrupt */
99: 
100:   arm_ack_irq(irq);
101: 
102:   if (irq == NVIC_IRQ_PENDSV)
103:     {
104: #ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_HIPRI_INTERRUPT
105:       /* Dispatch the PendSV interrupt */
106: 
107:       irq_dispatch(irq, regs);
108: #endif
109: #ifndef CONFIG_DISABLE_SIGNALS
110:       if (tcb && tcb->sigdeliver && !tcb->xcp.saved_regs)
111:         {
112:           /* Pendsv able to access running tcb with no critical section */
113: 
114:           up_schedule_sigaction(tcb);
115:         }
116: #endif
117: 
118:       up_irq_save();
119:     }
120:   else
121:     {
122:       irq_dispatch(irq, regs);
123:     }

125:   tcb = this_task();
126: 
127:   if (*running_task != tcb)
128:     {
129: #ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_ADDRENV
130:       /* Make sure that the address environment for the previously
131:        * running task is closed down gracefully (data caches dump,
132:        * MMU flushed) and set up the address environment for the new
133:        * thread at the head of the ready-to-run list.
134:        */
135: 
136:       addrenv_switch(tcb);
137:       tcb = this_task();
138: #endif

140:       /* Record the new "running" task when context switch occurred.
141:        * g_running_tasks[] is only used by assertion logic for reporting
142:        * crashes.
143:        */
144: 
145:       *running_task = tcb;
146:     }

149:

152:   regs = tcb->xcp.regs;
153: #endif

96: /****************************************************************************
97:  * Name: nx_smp_start
98:  *
99:  * Description:
100:  *   In an SMP configuration, only one CPU is initially active (CPU 0).
101:  *   System initialization occurs on that single thread. At the completion
102:  *   of the initialization of the OS, just before beginning normal
103:  *   multitasking, the additional CPUs would be started by calling this
104:  *   function.
105:  *
106:  * Input Parameters:
107:  *   None
108:  *
109:  * Returned Value:
110:  *   Zero on success; a negated errno value on failure.
111:  *
112:  * Assumption:
113:  *   Runs before the full initialization sequence has completed.  Runs after
114:  *   all OS facilities are set up, but before multi-tasking has been started.
115:  *
116:  ****************************************************************************/
117: 
118: int nx_smp_start(void)
119: {
120:   int ret;
121:   int cpu;
122: 
123:   /* Flush dcache before start other CPUs. */
124: 
125:   up_flush_dcache_all();
126: 
127:   /* Start all of the other CPUs.  CPU0 is already running. */
128: 
129:   for (cpu = 1; cpu < CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS; cpu++)
130:     {
131:       /* Start the CPU */
132: 
133:       ret = up_cpu_start(cpu);
134:       if (ret < 0)
135:         {
136:           serr("ERROR: Failed to start CPU%d: %d\n", cpu, ret);
137:           return ret;
138:         }
139:     }
140: 
141:   return OK;
142: }
143: 
144: #endif /* CONFIG_SMP */

# 4. IRQ vector and exception-entry structure

The runtime vector table is defined in:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_vectors.c:45-52`

```c
const vector_t _vectors[NR_IRQS] =
{
  [0]       = __idle_stack_top,
  [1]       = __start,
  [2 ... 14] = exception_common,
  [15 ...]   = exception_direct,
};
```

This is decisive:

- PendSV is IRQ 14 and uses `exception_common`.
- SysTick is IRQ 15 and uses `exception_direct`.

## SysTick path

```text
SysTick exception entry
  -> exception_direct
      -> arm_ack_irq(15)
      -> irq_dispatch(15, NULL)
          -> bk7258_timerisr
              -> nxsched_process_timer
              -> detail3 = 2
      -> compare running task state
      -> possibly pend PendSV
      -> return with EXC_RETURN
  -> normal thread execution resumes
      -> stage 27 can execute
```

`exception_direct()` is at `0x02159074`:

```asm
push {r3,r4,r5,lr}
mrs  r4, IPSR
...
mov  r0, r4
bl   arm_ack_irq
...
mov  r0, r4
movs r1, #0
bl   irq_dispatch
...
compare g_running_tasks[cpu] with g_assignedtasks[cpu]
...
if different:
    up_trigger_irq(PendSV, 0)
...
pop {..., lr}
bx   lr
```

The SysTick handler does not call `arm_doirq()` and does not execute the full software context-save path.

## PendSV path

PendSV vector 14 enters `exception_common`, then:

```text
exception_common
  -> save hardware/software/FPU context
  -> arm_doirq(14, regs)
      -> tcb->xcp.regs = regs
      -> nxsched_suspend_scheduler()
      -> board_autoled_on(LED_INIRQ)
      -> arm_ack_irq(14)
      -> PendSV-specific scheduler/signal logic
      -> possibly task selection
      -> nxsched_resume_scheduler()
      -> board_autoled_off(LED_INIRQ)
      -> tcb->xcp.regs = NULL
      -> return selected regs
  -> restore registers, BASEPRI, CONTROL, PSP/MSP, PSPLIM
  -> bx EXC_RETURN
```

`exception_common` is at `0x02159472`; `arm_doirq` is at `0x021590d0`.

# 8. PendSV and context-switch behavior after the ISR

After `irq_dispatch()` returns, `exception_direct()` compares:

- `g_running_tasks[cpu]`
- `g_assignedtasks[cpu]`

The ELF locations are:

```text
g_running_tasks:  0x280283dc
g_assignedtasks: 0x280283e8
```

This is the post-direct-IRQ scheduling handoff:

```c

  {
    up_trigger_irq(NVIC_IRQ_PENDSV, 0);
  }
```

The ARMv8-M implementation uses equivalent compiled logic in `exception_direct()`.

If the pointers differ:

1. `up_trigger_irq(NVIC_IRQ_PENDSV, 0)` writes the PendSV pending bit.
2. The SysTick handler returns from `exception_direct()`.
3. The Cortex-M exception controller may tail-chain directly into PendSV instead of returning to thread mode.
4. PendSV enters `exception_common`.
5. `arm_doirq()` performs the scheduler/context-switch processing.
6. Only after PendSV completes can the interrupted `up_cpu_start()` code execute stage 27.

Thus stage 27 does not prove merely that the SysTick ISR returned. It proves that the whole sequence before the stage-27 instruction returned to the CPU0 thread, including any immediately required PendSV processing.

A task mismatch is not expected merely because `nxsched_process_timer()` ran. On the first tick, the system is still inside `nx_smp_start()` in `nx_start()`, before normal `nx_bringup()`:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/sched/init/nx_start.c:805-826`

At that point the main active tasks should still be the idle tasks. This makes an unexpected `g_running_tasks`/`g_assignedtasks` mismatch less likely, but it remains the key branch to verify with a debugger or additional trace.

# 9. Stack limit, interrupt stack, and MPU

## Interrupt-stack layout

The linker map gives:

```text
__intstacks_start = 0x2802ac80
__intstacks_end   = 0x2802bc80
```

The build asserts two 2048-byte stacks:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/ld.script.tmp:153-156`

CPU0 interrupt stack:

```text
0x2802ac80 .. 0x2802b480
```

CPU1 interrupt stack:

```text
0x2802b480 .. 0x2802bc80
```

The BK-specific `up_get_intstackbase()` is:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_cpuidlestack.c:31-35`

```c
return g_bk7258_intstacks + cpu * INTSTACK_SIZE;
```

## CPU0 startup stack setup

`__start()` initially sets:

```asm
msr msplim, __idle_stack_base
```

Then `bk7258_start()` calls `arm_initialize_stack()` after CPU-private setup.

`arm_initialize_stack()` sets:

- MSP to the current CPU’s interrupt-stack top;
- MSPLIM to the current CPU’s interrupt-stack base;
- PSP appropriately;
- PSPLIM appropriately when hardware stack checking is enabled.

For CPU0, the initial runtime interrupt stack is therefore separate from the CPU0 idle thread stack.

## SysTick versus common exception stack handling

For SysTick through `exception_direct`:

- the processor performs normal hardware exception stacking;
- handler mode uses MSP;
- the direct C handler pushes `{r4, lr}`;
- there is no software save of FPU/nonvolatile registers;
- there is no software manipulation of MSPLIM/PSPLIM;
- there is no `tcb->xcp.regs`.

For PendSV through `exception_common`:

- the assembly explicitly disables the active stack limit while reserving software exception context;
- it saves the previous stack-limit value in the context;
- it restores MSP/PSP and MSPLIM/PSPLIM from the selected context;
- it restores BASEPRI and CONTROL;
- it exits via `bx lr` using EXC_RETURN.

The common epilogue is:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/arch/arm/src/arm_m/arm_exception.S:298-337`

The current ELF disassembly is at `0x02159472`.

## MPU

The MPU is initialized before `nx_start()` in:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_start.c:107-149`

The relevant regions include:

- AP flash, read-only;
- AP RAM, read/write, inner-shareable, non-cacheable;
- AP spinlock area `0x28000000`;
- CP RAM;
- mailbox buffers;
- optional PSRAM;
- device region at `0x40000000`.

The spinlock and boottrace regions are explicitly covered by the AP spinlock MPU region:

```text
BK7258_AP_SPINLOCK_BASE = 0x28000000
BK7258_AP_SPINLOCK_SIZE = 0x00010000
```

There is no obvious MPU mapping defect in the direct SysTick path. A stack-limit or MPU fault remains possible during automatic exception unstacking or a later PendSV restore, but `detail3=2` proves that the C ISR body itself completed.

## Candidate 1: Atomic-gate spin in the immediate post-ISR PendSV trigger

This is the strongest concrete post-`detail3=2` software candidate, conditional on a task mismatch.

The post-dispatch code can call:

```text
exception_direct
  -> up_trigger_irq(PendSV)
  -> modifyreg32(NVIC_INTCTRL, ...)
  -> atomic_lock()
```

`modifyreg32()` uses a global spinlock:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/arch/arm/src/common/arm_modifyreg.c:94-104`

The ELF implementation at `0x02159370` uses:

```text
atomic_fetch_add_4()
atomic_load_4()
wait until owner/turn condition
```

`atomic_lock()` is at `0x0215d138` and loops until the BK7258 hwspinlock operation succeeds.

The current gate is the AP-only Peterson implementation:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_hwspinlock.c`

The current build no longer uses the old three-core SRAM-exclusive implementation, but CPU0 and CPU1 can still contend for this software gate. A failed `atomic_lock()` is an unbounded loop.

Why it fits:

- `detail3=2` proves all timer-body atomics completed.
- The next potentially blocking code is the post-dispatch mismatch path.
- Stage 27 is not written until after `exception_direct` returns.
- `up_trigger_irq()` calls `modifyreg32()`, which can spin indefinitely.
- The gate has diagnostic `detail4` values specifically intended to identify this path.

What would strengthen this diagnosis:

- `detail4` ending in one of the Peterson-gate markers while primary remains 26;
- debugger PC in `atomic_lock()`, `bk7258_hwspinlock_trylock()`, or `modifyreg32()`;
- `g_running_tasks[0] != g_assignedtasks[0]`.

Important qualification: if the two task pointers are equal, this path is not entered.

## Candidate 2: PendSV tail-chain or PendSV context-switch path

This is closely related to Candidate 1 but includes the full exception/context-switch path.

If `exception_direct()` observes a task mismatch, it pends PendSV. The processor may tail-chain from SysTick directly into PendSV. Stage 27 cannot execute until PendSV completes.

Potential blocking points include:

1. `board_autoled_on(LED_INIRQ)`;
2. `arm_doirq()` scheduler suspension/resumption;
3. signal handling;
4. atomic/spinlock operations in scheduler code;
5. `board_autoled_off(LED_INIRQ)`;
6. common exception context restore;
7. PSP/MSP/PSPLIM restoration;
8. automatic exception return.

Evidence:

- `exception_direct()` at `0x02159074` explicitly pends PendSV on a task mismatch.
- PendSV vector 14 uses `exception_common`.
- `arm_doirq()` stores `tcb->xcp.regs`, performs scheduler operations, and clears it on exit.
- `arm_doirq()` invokes LED hooks.
- The build has SMP, RR scheduling, signals, FPU, MPU, and hardware stack checking.

The LED subpath is particularly concrete:

```text
board_autoled_on()
  -> bk7258_gpio_write()
      -> modifyreg32()
          -> atomic_lock()
```

However, because SysTick itself uses `exception_direct`, the LED hooks are not involved until a PendSV or another common exception is entered.

This candidate is less likely than a direct atomic spin if the first tick occurs exactly during `nx_smp_start()` with both CPUs still assigned to idle tasks. At that point, there should normally be no task switch to request.

## Candidate 3: Immediate interrupt re-entry/starvation after `up_irq_restore()`

Stage 27 is after:

```asm
msr BASEPRI, r8
```

and there is no barrier before the stage-27 call.

Once BASEPRI is restored, any pending or newly arriving interrupt can be accepted before the trace write. Possibilities include:

- another SysTick;
- a mailbox IRQ;
- an IRQ caused by the CPU2 handshake or mailbox activity;
- PendSV if it was pended by `exception_direct()`.

This can delay stage 27 or, in an interrupt-storm situation, starve the thread indefinitely.

Evidence:

- Stage 25 is deliberately written before interrupt restoration.
- The mailbox pending bit is explicitly cleared before stage 25:
  `bk7258_cpustart.c:234-238`.
- The first interrupt is nevertheless SysTick, not mailbox.
- `up_irq_restore()` is exactly the operation immediately preceding stage 27.
- The SysTick is enabled at `bk7258_timerisr.c:70-81`.

This is a plausible explanation for a trace that remains at primary 26 even though `detail3=2`, but a normal 1 kHz SysTick should not repeatedly preempt the few instructions needed to reach stage 27. It becomes more credible if the SysTick is re-pending immediately because of a hardware/reload/configuration issue or if another IRQ continuously reasserts.

## Candidate 4: Fault during automatic SysTick exception unstacking

`detail3=2` is written before `exception_direct()` returns. The automatic hardware exception return has not yet happened.

The direct handler returns through:

```asm
pop {r3,r4,r5,lr}
bx  lr
```

where `lr` is the EXC_RETURN value.

A MemManage, BusFault, UsageFault, SecureFault, or HardFault during exception unstacking would leave primary at 26 and detail3 at 2.

Possible causes would include:

- corrupted hardware-stacked frame;
- invalid return EXC_RETURN;
- MSP/PSP corruption;
- stack-limit violation;
- corrupted xPSR/PC;
- memory access failure while unstacking.

Why it is lower ranked:

- `exception_direct()` saves and restores LR in a simple, visible sequence.
- SysTick does not manipulate `tcb->xcp.regs`, PSP, PSPLIM, or the software context frame.
